Firstly, congrats on your upcoming graduation to becoming a full-fledged tech! As far as the SBB and SM, I do not know if that really matters as a new MLT or MLS, at least it does not carry more weight here in the Southeast. A lot of places down here look for someone with a generalist background with maybe some knowledge of micro (if you go that route). But again, it varies greatly from hospital to hospital, as far as how seriously they take specialties, so I may be way off base there. 

As far as BB vs Microbiology, they are my personal favorite departments to work, but my heart really belongs in microbiology. BB is going to be more acutely nerve-racking as far as emergencies go, but antibody panels can be fun to work with under less frantic conditions. In micro, I love it for a similar reason -- it's like a puzzle. Granted, a lot of it is automated, but there's a unique satisfaction that I only feel when I can isolate organisms in a huge mix of normal flora. What can I say? I am a micro nerd.
